discovery_review.summary: The diff implements a reasonable opt-in truncation feature with tests and docs, but it ships the exact configuration shape (option name, character-based units, zero-means-disabled semantics, and the truncation marker text) without any evidence that the designated decision-owner reviewed or approved these specifics, even though the retrieved decision notes explicitly require that sign-off before shipping.

findings.question: Has Lina Imani actually confirmed the limit units (characters), the meaning of 0 (disabled), the truncation marker text/format, and the exact ini option name (junit_logging_truncation_limit) before this change ships?
findings.why: The compatibility decision notes explicitly state 'Lina Imani owns the reporting behavior decision; ask her to confirm the limit units, zero meaning and truncation marker before shipping' and that 'the exact setting name and limit units have not been approved yet.' The implementation unilaterally picks all of these (character-based limit, default '0' = disabled, a custom '...[N chars truncated]...' marker, and the name junit_logging_truncation_limit) with no evidence in the diff or task notes that this required approval was obtained, only a tracking ticket marked Done whose resolution doesn't confirm the actual design was reviewed.
